# 0verpg
Small Dungeon Based Game that is cross-platform available.

### Features

🗡️ Dungeon exploration

👾 RPG-style gameplay

⚔️ Turn-based combat

🎒 Equipment - Armour, Weapon, Potion, Spell, Skill systems

🧙 Choose from multiple character classes

💀 Monster encounters, defeat increasingly powerful enemies

📈 Character progression and equip class-specific gear

🏆 Loot collection

🗺️ Randomized dungeon adventures

⌨️ Lightweight terminal/console interface

🖥️ Cross-platform support (Linux, BSD, MacOS and Windows)

🚀 Written entirely in modern C++20

⚔️ Level up and improve your hero

---

# Compile

```bash
make -j8 # to use 8 cores/threads in parallel compile
cp -r .0verpg.json ~/
sudo make install
```

### Don't forget to copy `.0verpg.json` to `~/` . If you are `root` user, the config must be copied to /root/ and edited there.

The game first looks for `.0verpg.json` in the current directory, so you can also run `./0verpg en` straight from the repository without copying it. A `.0verpg.json` in the current directory takes priority over the one in `~/`.

Now to run the game type `0verpg en` this will use the English version. Currently there are three languages `en`, `bg` - Bulgarian and `it` - Italian.

### Don't forget to use the `Spells key` after start to change with the +5 attacking power spell. Otherwise it will default only to the hero attacking power and `Basic Spell`.

## MacOS users

Thanks to [@lasers](https://github.com/lasers) for the help to make the compile process easier and avoid the header `iostream` not to be found.

Here is what it looked like:

> 5\. ~/src/su8-0verpg on main 
>     ❯ g++  -o 0verpg main.cpp -g2 -Wall -Wextra -O2 -std=c++20 -D_DEFAULT_SOURCE -pipe -pedantic -Wundef -Wshadow -W -Wwrite-strings -Wcast-align -Wstrict-overflow=5 -Wconversion -Wpointer-arith -Wformat=2 -Wsign-compare -Wendif-label
>     s -Wredundant-decls -Winit-self
>     main.cpp:18:10: fatal error: 'iostream' file not found
>        18 | #include <iostream>
>           |          ^~~~~~~~~~
>     1 error generated.

To fix this just type:

```bash
clang++ -isystem "$(xcrun --show-sdk-path)/usr/include/c++/v1" -std=c++20 -O2 -Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic -Wconversion -Wshadow main.cpp -o 0verpg
```

## Windows users

Tested with [Visual Studio Code Editor](https://code.visualstudio.com/download), but you need to install [MingW](https://github.com/niXman/mingw-builds-binaries/releases/download/16.2.0-rt_v14-rev1/x86_64-16.2.0-release-posix-seh-ucrt-rt_v14-rev1.7z), once downloaded extract it to **C:\MingW**, then re-open [Visual Studio Code Editor](https://code.visualstudio.com/download), you might want to install C\C++ extensions if you plan to write C\C++ code with the editor. If you plan to contribute to this project go to **File->Preferences->Settings** and type to search for **cppStandard** and set it to c17 to both C++ and C.

I use **One Monokai** theme for the [VScode Editor](https://code.visualstudio.com/download)

In [Visual Studio Code Editor](https://code.visualstudio.com/download), go to **Terminal->Configure Tasks...->Create tasks.json from template** and copy and paste this into it:

```json
{
  "version": "2.0.0",
  "tasks": [
    {
        "type": "cppbuild",
        "label": "C/C++",
        "command": "C:\\MingW\\bin\\g++.exe",
        "args": [
            "-fdiagnostics-color=always",
            "-std=c++20",
            "-ggdb",
            "-lpthread",
            "-D_DEFAULT_SOURCE",
            "-Wall",
            "-Wextra",
            "-O2",
            "-pipe",
            "-pedantic",
            "-Wundef",
            "-Wshadow",
            "-W",
            "-Wwrite-strings",
            "-Wcast-align",
            "-Wstrict-overflow=5",
            "-Wconversion",
            "-Wpointer-arith",
            "-Wformat=2",
            "-Wsign-compare",
            "-Wendif-labels",
            "-Wredundant-decls",
            "-Winit-self",
            "${file}",
            "-o",
            "${fileDirname}/${fileBasenameNoExtension}"
        ],
        "options": {
            "cwd": "C:\\MingW\\bin"
        },
        "problemMatcher": [
            "$gcc"
        ],
        "group": {
            "kind": "build",
            "isDefault": true
        },
        "detail": "compiler: C:\\MingW\\bin\\g++.exe"
    }
]
}
```

### Don't forget to copy `.0verpg.json` to the `C:\MingW\Bin\` folder too.

### To compile the game press **CTRL** + **SHIFT** + **B** , then from the same folder start the `0verpg.bat` script.

Optioanlly if you want to play the game from VSCode's console -- wait until it compiles, after that press **CTRL** + **\`** and paste this `cp -r C:\Users\YOUR_USERNAME_GOES_HERE\Desktop\main.exe C:\MingW\bin;cd C:\MingW\bin;.\main.exe`
